title: Short Stuff: James Polk, Disinterred
summary: Short Stuff episode on former U.S. President James K. Polk and the unusual story of his remains being moved several times after his death. The hosts cover his early career (Tennessee State Senate clerk, Speaker of the Tennessee House, Governor of Tennessee), his presidency (1845-1849) including the Independent Treasury System, the Naval Academy, the Smithsonian bill, the first US postage stamp, and the Mexican-American War. They then describe his death, likely from cholera, his first burial in the Nashville City Cemetery among cholera victims, his reinterment at Polk Place per his will, the sale and demolition of Polk Place after his widow Sarah's death, and the state of Tennessee disinterring him and moving him to the State Capitol. Finally they discuss the 2017 push by State Senator Joey Hensley to move him to his presidential library in Columbia, Tennessee, which passed the State Senate but was blocked by the Tennessee Historical Commission, and a 2018 Senate vote that failed by one vote.

segments.title: Introduction and Polk's early career
segments.summary: Hosts introduce James K. Polk, covering his start as a Tennessee State Senate clerk, his time as Speaker of the Tennessee House and Governor, and his birth in North Carolina and move to Tennessee.

segments.title: Polk's presidency
segments.summary: Polk's election over Henry Clay-era rival Taylor (as spoken, Tyler is the named opponent in the discussion, though the transcript garbles the name), his one-term promises, and accomplishments: the Naval Academy, first US postage stamp, Smithsonian law, and the Independent Treasury System, plus the Mexican-American War.

segments.title: Polk's death and first burial
segments.summary: Polk is believed to have died of cholera after being surrounded by cholera cases. He was first interred in the Nashville City Cemetery with cholera victims, which the hosts say was required for people who died of infectious disease.

segments.title: Reinterment at Polk Place and its sale
segments.summary: After complaints, Polk was reinterred at Polk Place, his Nashville mansion, per his will, with a memorial in the front yard. After Sarah Polk died about forty-two years later, Polk Place was sold to a developer and demolished, a dispute arising over a will clause that Tennessee deemed unenforceable.

segments.title: Disinterment and move to the State Capitol
segments.summary: The state of Tennessee disinterred Polk and Sarah and moved their remains to the State Capitol in Nashville. The hosts note he is overshadowed by the Jackson and Johnson monuments.
topics: Andrew Jackson and Andrew Johnson monuments

segments.title: Push to move Polk to Columbia, Tennessee
segments.summary: In 2017 State Senator Joey Hensley pushed to move Polk to his presidential library at his father's house in Columbia, Tennessee. The bill passed the State Senate in March but the Tennessee Historical Commission opposed it, and in 2018 a Senate vote failed by one vote. Family members are divided.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts close with a note about visiting Nashville and sign off the show.
